traffic_rule: No signal crosses a group cut: each PC's boundary pins (row/col/data/strb in, rdata/rvalid out) sit in its own window and connect only to its own controller (ot_hbm_svc_pc_ctrl_leaf); groups are whole HBM3 channels (PC pairs). The only shared macro pins today are clk and rst_n (window 16), replaced by one clk/rst_n per slice.
plan_delta: PHY_N -> PHY_NW / PHY_NC / PHY_NE abutting hard partitions, cuts at x = 2272.32 / 6523.2 um (8.64 grid), each holding one slice macro
L63 / L63m and L114 / L114m split 8|8 PCs: the W (E) half follows the L8/L21 (L8m/L21m) path T055->T059->T060W (T056->T061->T060E); the C half keeps the vsN6 path
L22 / L22m leave PHY_NC via T060C->T057 (today they leave from the W/E side): no new region pair, bits only
bus bit order fixed by PC (composer): the bundles carry whole PCs

pg_bump.core_grid: opentallas.core_bumps.v1 150-um VDD/VSS checkerboard (pg_bumps.json) skips the PHY io windows: unchanged
pg_bump.phy_domain: each slice keeps the PHY domain's own 45-um micro-bump rows under its PC windows (package side, blackbox to the core flow); cuts fall on channel-pair boundaries, so no channel's DQ/CA bumps straddle a cut (ASSUMED: the IP's bump map is per channel)
pg_bump.straps: each slice macro keeps the M4 VDD/VSS straps (OBS M1-M4) over its own width; parent M5 stripes via-in per slice (same rule as today)
pg_bump.power: 10.48 W per stack (1.2 TB/s x 0.8 pJ/bit + 2.8 W idle, hbm_b2_power.py, ASSUMED basis) split by PC count: W 2.62 / C 5.24 / E 2.62 W

generator_variant: opt-in hbm_phy_gen.py --variant rc_slice --pcs LO-HI (default rc unchanged, byte-identical): same per-PC pins and windows, footprint = the group's windows snapped up to 8.64 (246 / 492 units), clk/rst_n in the group's middle window; ROOT-MERGE (shared tool)
assumptions: the licensed HBM3E PHY supports per-channel-group (4-channel) clocking with one clock input per group; stack-global functions (IEEE1500 test port, temperature, global reset) live in the C slice
region insertion scaled from the equal-thirds split by the half-width change (mk_feed_c23.py)
